title: Sneaking into the district: Joe Oliver and Grunwald's Cave
summary: As a violin student Levy follows bands and sneaks into the district to hear Joe Oliver and a jazz band at Grunwald's Cave.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, you know, I was studying violin and the teacher didn't want us to play anything but the classical music, but I'd follow like all the other kids. I'd follow the bands down the street and once in a while sneak in the district, you know, with my long pants on and listen to them. I stood on the corner and listened to Joe Oliver and the bands, you know, in the district.
Is that so? Yeah, I sneaked in there. Where'd you hear Joe play? Do you remember that?

I think he was right on the corner, right on the, what's that, Pete Lalo? Yes. I remember him and then. Corner place near the station, huh? Yeah, it was, what was it, Iperville Street? It was where the district was. I wasn't supposed to be there, but I sneaked in. And I had two three kids. One of them was studying saxophone, a couple of them studying violin, and one was studying bass. We were all interested, crazy about music, you know. And oh yeah, we used to go down the, halfway down the stairs there, they did Grunwald's Cave. There was a jazz band playing there in those days, Grunwald's Cave. And we, and we, yes, we, I remember walking down the stairs and we could hear this, and then the drummer he was writing came and the trumpet was playing all these extra notes, you know. And it was wonderful to our ears, you know, because studying the classical music played exactly what was on the paper, see. Yeah. And these other guys had a living and putting extra notes in, and that sounded like heaven to us. Do you remember who any of them were? I think it was the, I'm pretty sure it was the original Dixon Land band, Tony Ladder and all the, what was it, who was with that band? Nick?
